n.description: Number of items to be packed

source.citation: J.M. Valério de Carvalho, "Exact solution of bin-packing problems using column generation and branch-and-bound," Annals of Operations Research 86 (1999) 629-659.

notes: carvalho1999 (Section 1) states the general bin-packing problem at the level of individual items: bins of capacity $W$ and a list of $n$ items of integer sizes $l_0,\ldots,l_{n-1}$; this is the parametrization used here and by formulation `a` (the classical Martello-Toth formulation). Formulations `b` (Gilmore-Gomory patterns) and `c` (arc-flow) instead work with items aggregated by distinct size into $(m, w, b)$; their `gen_params.py` derives this aggregation from $(W, n, l)$.
We add implicit assumptions that W >= 1 and n >= 1.

The source paper's arc reduction criteria (Criteria 1-4) and valid inequalities (Propositions 2.2, 2.3), used in formulation `c`'s underlying arc-flow model, are solver-side optimizations and are not part of the base MILP formulation (Equations 7-11); we formulate the full, unreduced arc set there.

The FrontierOR source instances (`instance/*.json`) use a much larger bin capacity and item count than is tractable for a Lean formulation; `data.json` instead uses a small, hand-verified instance in the same schema.
